note: Dialog sentences BOTH surfaces print, as prose segments: a string is constant words, an object is a name each surface draws as a chip (`quoted` says the plain-text spelling wraps it in straight double quotes). Read by `the_two_surfaces_build_every_shared_sentence_from_the_same_segments` in crates/dux-core/src/prose.rs and by prose.test.tsx in crates/dux-web/web. Adjacent strings are merged before comparing, so either side may split its constant words however it likes; the words and the names must be the same. Paths are outside any home directory because the terminal side home-collapses them.

cases.what: detaching an agent with one running tab
segments: dux will ask
to shut down and wait up to 30 seconds for it to exit before forcing it. The agent stays in the list as Detached, and you can resume it later. Anything the agent is doing right now is interrupted.

cases.what: detaching an agent with several running tabs
segments: dux will ask

to shut down and wait up to 45 seconds for it to exit before forcing it. The agent stays in the list as Detached, and you can resume it later. Anything the agent is doing right now is interrupted. All 3 running tabs stop together.

cases.what: recreating a working copy under a running Claude tab
segments: Recreate the working copy for this agent at

?

If branch
still exists locally, dux checks it out there again. If it is gone locally but still on the remote, dux creates it again from
, holding everything that had been pushed. If it is gone everywhere, dux creates it again from

, and the commits that branch held are not coming back.

Any code changes that were in the old directory are gone either way: this puts the directory back, not its contents. The conversation may resume, because the agent's CLI keys its history by directory path and dux recreates the working copy at the same path.

A running
tab keeps working in the recreated copy by itself. A terminal still open in the old directory keeps working in a directory that is gone; close it and open one in the recreated copy.
